newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL PRIVATE COFFEE SECTOR TO MEET AUGUST 18.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL PRIVATE COFFEE SECTOR TO MEET AUGUST 18.

text.p: Private sector members of Brazil's coffee council, the CDPC, will meet in Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais state, on August 18 to discuss general issues affecting the sector, a producer official said.

"We are still working on the agenda but the meeting should cover the whole sector - the soluble industry, producers, domestic roasters," said Rui Queiroz, president of the coffee committee at the National Agriculture Confederation (CNA).

Members of the CDPC including government representatives last held a meeting in Brasilia on July 29 in preparation for the next full session of the council scheduled to be held in Santos but for which no date has yet been set.

One of the key talking points in recent meetings has been how to tackle problems besetting the soluble coffee industry, which officials say is losing competitiveness to other producers because of the high cost of raw materials within Brazil.
Council members have discussed a plan to lend up to 770,000 60-kg bags of poorer-quality government coffee stocks to the industry, repayable in kind over three years.
But the plan has become the subject of debate between the Finance and the Industry and Commerce Ministries and there has been no decision on the issue, a Finance Ministry official said.
